title: Deferred Archive Proxy and Correlated Snapshot Mosaic for On-call Diagnostics
author: Nadia Patel
release_notes: Add deferred archive proxy to reduce hot-retrieval load on the primary blobstore; introduce Correlated Snapshot Mosaic (CSM) format for compact per-incident archives; migration adds a background reingestion job to build mosaics for last 90 days; no user-facing API changes; rollout via staged canary and grace period of 48 hours.
description: Context and motivation: On-call workflows increasingly rely on compact incident snapshots that combine logs, traces, metrics, and runbook fragments. Large, immediate retrievals against the primary archive cause increased tail latency and occasional rate-limited errors during high-volume incidents. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: a Deferred Archive Proxy that schedules and serves pre-assembled archive mosaics, and a Correlated Snapshot Mosaic (CSM) format that packs heterogeneous artifacts into a compact, seekable index for sub-second partial retrievals. Design: The Deferred Archive Proxy sits in front of the existing blobstore and metadata index. It records retrieval intents, schedules assembly work during low-cost windows, and serves mosaics from a cache tier (S3 with lifecycle policy) with an LRU eviction policy. The CSM format is a small contiguous file containing a lightweight index (artifact type, time bounds, byte offsets, CRC) and concatenated gzipped chunks. The proxy supports partial reads by responding with range-aware streaming. Implementation details: - New service archive/proxy implemented in Go using the existing fetcher framework; exposes internal-only endpoints /v1/intent and /v1/mosaic/{id}. - Background assembler worker that reads existing artifact streams, normalizes encodings, compresses per-artifact, and writes a CSM with an index JSON blob prepended. - Migration job archive/migration/reingest that walks recent incidents, enqueues intents for mosaics, and marks legacy snapshots as archived. - SDK helpers in scripts/diagnostics to request intents and to fetch partial slices for debugging CLIs. - Telemetry: new metrics archive.proxy.requests, archive.proxy.assemble_duration_bucket, archive.csm.size_bytes, and SLO-oriented error tags. - Security: mosaics respect existing RBAC checks; assembler runs under existing build-worker role. Testing and rollout: - Unit tests for serializer/deserializer and partial-range reads. - Integration tests with the diagnostics sandbox (local mode) that validate partial retrieval latency under synthetic load. - Load tests: synthetic replay of 1k concurrent snapshot reads shows 65% reduction in direct blobstore read rate and 2.1x reduction in p95 latency for debug CLIs when mosaics are available. - Rollout plan: enable proxy in staging for 48h; deploy canary to 10% of production hosts for 72h with traffic mirroring; enable background reingestion for last 7 days first, then expand to 30/90 day windows. Migration: - Background reingestion job is idempotent and runs as a low-priority batch job; it annotates incidents with mosaic_id when complete. - A migration flag controls whether the proxy will fall back to live assembly vs serving mosaics. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: assembler bugs could produce corrupted mosaics. Mitigation: assembler writes to a temporary key and validates CRCs before atomically renaming; integration test validates round-trip. - Risk: increased storage cost for duplicated data. Mitigation: lifecycle rules expire mosaics older than 90 days by default; we can reduce retention per-team. Checklist: - [x] Serializer and deserializer for CSM format - [x] Deferred proxy endpoints and routing - [x] Background assembler and worker queue integration - [x] SDK helper scripts and CLI examples - [x] Telemetry and dashboard (dashboard links included in commit) - [x] Migration job and rollout plan - [x] Security review by infra team Commits summary: "chore: add CSM format and serializer; feat(archive): proxy service and intent endpoint; feat(archive): assembler worker and queue consumer; test: add integration and load tests; docs: rollout plan and dashboard links; ci: add pipeline steps for assembly integration tests".
commits_summary: 7 commits: initial csm serializer and format spec; proxy service scaffolding; assembler worker and queue integration; background reingest job; CLI helpers and tests; dashboards and alert tweaks; docs and rollout notes.
review_comments: Eliot Mendez: Great separation of concerns. One concern: the index is JSON prepended to the file, that could complicate streaming parsers. Consider a fixed 64-byte header that points to index offset so streaming readers can seek without scanning.
Nadia Patel (author): Good point, Eliot. I changed the format to include a fixed 64-byte binary header with magic/version/offset. Updated serializer accordingly in serializer.go.
Priya Rao: How does RBAC get enforced for partial reads? We need to ensure the proxy checks the same backend predicate so we don't leak internal-only artifacts.
Nadia Patel (author): Proxy delegates to metadata service on request start and caches auth decisions for 5 minutes; added tests to validate enforcement and a note in the docs.
Jasper Lin: Load tests look promising. Suggest adding a metric for cache hit ratio so we can monitor adoption.
Nadia Patel (author): Added archive.proxy.cache_hit_ratio and dashboard panels in dashboards/archive-mosaic.json.
notes: Merged after infra approval. Canary rollout completed with 0 critical regressions reported. Observability dashboard added to the SLO toolkit space.
